cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Try It First
cards.instruction: Get someone else to test the shortcut, substitute, or questionable fix before you rely on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Taste this coffee substitute before I fill my cup. A small sip, please; we're assessing flavour, not thirst.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We have proper coffee. Why should I spoil breakfast?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A sample is not a serving. One spoonful, then water to clear your palate; I'll make proper coffee if it fails.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You take the spoonful. Your cup's empty too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It stays empty until I have a result. Please use the clean spoon; I can't assess your reaction if you're tasting yesterday's coffee as well.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 sample size and A3 palate procedure make A expert test director while keeping A cup empty until B tries the substitute.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 breakfast concern causes A3 small sample; B4 role swap causes A5 insistence on a result, then a new dirty-spoon concern.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants proper coffee and B4 challenges the one-sided test rather than passively tasting.

heightening.evidence: A5 maintains the asymmetry but introduces yesterday coffee as an unnecessary fresh testing issue.

specificity.evidence: A1 substitute and B4 empty cups are sufficient; A5 assumes an old-coffee spoon not otherwise established.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 spoon-history explanation distracts from B4 direct invitation to taste first.

coach2.stated: A1 substitute pending; B2 proper coffee exists; B4 both cups empty; A5 adds old-coffee contamination.
coach2.inferred: A intends B to test before A commits a serving.
coach2.missing: The dirty-spoon history is unnecessary to explain why A refuses first taste.
coach2.firstDefect: A5 introduces yesterday coffee instead of responding specifically to the proposed role swap.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 questions A1 substitute instead of proper coffee.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 reduces B2 sacrifice to a controlled sample.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 asks A to take A3 sample instead.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 refuses B4 role reversal but pivots to an unprepared spoon condition.
